name: Answer customer calls and contacts
summary: Customers of a city-owned electricity distributor phone the contact centre about bills, payments, moves, outages and service requests. An IVR routes each call to about 40 representatives who verify the caller, open the account in the customer information system and either answer on the spot or start work for another team: a move order, a billing investigation, a payment arrangement, a trouble call or a field order. The regulator requires 65% of calls answered within 30 seconds; in 2021 the centre took 186,632 calls, answered 83% on time and resolved 89% at first contact. Storms, rate changes and the summer move season bring call peaks that staffing cannot follow, and calls that need research turn into callbacks.

baseline.org_archetype: A municipally owned Ontario electricity distributor with about 350,000 customers, an in-house contact centre open weekdays and Saturdays, a CIS, an OMS and smart meters.
baseline.notes: 2020 had remote working and the lowest on-time answer rate of the period (74.6%); calls only, written contacts excluded.

unit_of_work: one customer call answered by an agent
trigger: A customer or member of the public calls the customer care line and asks for an agent.
end_state: The caller's question is answered or the follow-up work is created in the CIS or OMS, and the call is coded.

volume.seasonality: Higher from June to September (moves) and after November and May price changes; lower in December. Storm days bring short peaks (see surge).

evidence.note: 186,632 calls to agents in 2021, about 15,550 a month (src-scorecard); low and high are the author's estimate of monthly swing.

surge.cause: major storm (wind, ice storm, tornado or derecho)

evidence.note: Taken from the organisation file's surge for this process (May 2022 derecho, 180,000 customers out); outage calls dominate during a surge and the IVR outage message absorbs part of it.
40 representatives in the organisation file; about 27 FTE on calls after moves, written contacts, training and leave. Loaded cost = wage x 1.40.
Four supervisors; most of their time goes to escalations, call monitoring, scheduling and coaching. Loaded cost = wage x 1.40.

roles.title: Customer service manager (contact centre, billing and credit, metering)

evidence.note: One of three customer service managers; oversight of service levels and staffing. Has no step: management time is not modelled per call. Loaded cost = wage x 1.40.

systems.name: Contact centre telephony, IVR and call recording
Local meter data management and validation tool
Customer web portal, MyAccount, mobile app and outage map
Mobile workforce management and field tablets

steps.name: Call the customer care line
steps.description: A residential or business customer, or a member of the public reporting a hazard, dials the customer care number during contact centre hours (weekdays plus Saturday) or the 24-hour emergency option. The caller's own time is not counted as labour.

error.defect_description: None.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for an Ontario utility contact centre in 2019-2022 using a CIS, OMS and IVR; no published handle time was found.

steps.name: Route the call through the IVR
steps.description: The IVR plays any outage message for the caller's area, asks for the account or phone number, offers self-service balance and payment options and routes the caller to a skill queue (billing, moving, outage, collections). The volume counts only calls that reach an agent, so every case continues.
outputs: queued call with account number and reason

error.defect_description: Caller chooses the wrong menu option and lands in the wrong skill queue.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for an Ontario utility contact centre in 2019-2022 using a CIS, OMS and IVR; no published handle time was found.

steps.name: Answer the call and verify the caller
steps.description: The next free representative answers, reads the screen pop, and verifies the caller by name, service address and account number or postal code before discussing the account. If the caller is not the account holder the agent limits what can be disclosed.

error.defect_description: Caller verified on the wrong account with a similar name or address.

control.basis: OEB Distribution System Code s.7.6: 65% of qualified calls answered within 30 seconds and s.7.7 abandon rate of 10% or less, measured yearly

evidence.note: 83.14% of 186,632 calls answered within 30 s in 2021 and 74.60% in 2020 (src-scorecard); the triangular wait puts about 85% of calls under 30 s.

steps.name: Open the account and identify the reason for the call
steps.description: The representative opens the account in the CIS, scans the last bills, payments, notices and open orders, checks the outage map or OMS banner when the caller mentions power, and picks the reason code that decides how the call is handled.

error.defect_description: Wrong reason picked, so the caller is sent down the wrong path.

next.condition: question about a bill, usage or payment
payment by card, address, e-billing, pre-authorized or equal payment change
overdue balance, notice received or cannot pay
moving in, out or within the territory
power out, partial power, flicker or hazard
new service, upgrade, meter check, tree trimming or isolation request
angry caller or request to speak to a supervisor

evidence.note: Reason mix is the author's estimate for an Ontario utility with monthly billing; outage calls rise sharply during storms (see volume surge).

steps.name: Explain the bill and payment history
steps.description: The representative walks the caller through the charges, the time-of-use or tiered prices, usage compared with the same month last year from the smart meter data, and any late payment charge. Most callers accept the explanation; some dispute a charge and some need research the agent cannot finish on the call.

error.defect_description: Agent gives a wrong explanation of a charge or rate.

next.condition: caller disputes the usage or a charge
needs research or another department; callback promised

evidence.note: 89.04% of surveyed callers in 2021 said the issue was resolved at first contact (src-scorecard); split of unresolved cases is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check meter reads and usage for the disputed charge
steps.description: The representative opens the hourly smart meter data and read history, compares the disputed period with earlier months, and looks for estimated reads, a recent meter change or a move date that could explain the amount.

error.defect_description: Agent misses an estimated read or meter change.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for an Ontario utility contact centre in 2019-2022 using a CIS, OMS and IVR; no published handle time was found.

steps.name: Raise a billing investigation and close the call
steps.description: The representative creates a billing investigation task in the CIS with the period, the caller's concern and the evidence found, may hold collection activity on the disputed amount, tells the caller a billing analyst will reply, and records the call notes and disposition.

error.defect_description: Task raised with missing period or wrong category, so the analyst has to call back.

control.basis: OEB Distribution System Code s.7.8: written response to a qualified enquiry within 10 business days, 80% of the time

evidence.note: Response standard from src-dsc; handling is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Take a payment or update account details
steps.description: The representative transfers the caller to the secure card payment line or updates the mailing address, phone, e-billing, pre-authorized payment or equal payment plan in the CIS, and confirms the change back to the caller.

error.defect_description: Banking or address keyed wrongly.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for an Ontario utility contact centre in 2019-2022 using a CIS, OMS and IVR; no published handle time was found.

steps.name: Review the overdue balance and the caller's options
steps.description: The representative reviews the overdue amount, notices already sent, any security deposit, earlier payment agreements and whether the caller says they are on a low income, then decides with the caller between a payment arrangement and a referral to assistance programs.

error.defect_description: Customer not told of low-income options they qualify for.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for an Ontario utility contact centre in 2019-2022 using a CIS, OMS and IVR; no published handle time was found.

steps.name: Set up a payment extension or arrears payment agreement
steps.description: For a short delay the representative records a promise-to-pay date; for larger arrears the agent builds an arrears payment agreement in the CIS within the OEB minimum terms, quotes the down payment and instalments, suspends collection steps and records the call.

error.defect_description: Instalments set shorter than the OEB minimum or down payment above the cap.

control.basis: OEB Distribution System Code s.2.7: down payment up to 15% (10% for eligible low-income) and minimum terms of 5 or 10 months (8, 12 or 16 for eligible low-income)

evidence.note: Terms from src-dsc; handling time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Refer the caller to bill assistance programs
steps.description: The representative explains the Ontario Electricity Support Program, LEAP emergency assistance and, in 2020-2021, the COVID-19 Energy Assistance Program, gives the intake agency's contact, flags the account so collections waits, and records the call.

error.defect_description: Account not flagged, so a disconnection notice still goes out.

evidence.note: Programs listed in src-ban2020; handling time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Take the move details and check identity
steps.description: For a move the representative records the old and new addresses, move dates, landlord contact for renters, and for a new customer the date of birth and photo identification, and reminds the caller that ten business days' notice is asked for.

error.defect_description: Wrong move date or unit number recorded.

evidence.note: Information asked for and notice period from src-moving.

steps.name: Create the move order in the CIS
steps.description: The representative creates the move-out and move-in orders against the premise in the CIS, notes any security deposit question for the account team, and confirms the dates and set-up charge to the caller before closing the call.

error.defect_description: Order created on the wrong premise or unit.

evidence.note: Set-up charge from src-moving; time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check the outage map and OMS for a known outage
steps.description: The representative checks the OMS and outage map for the caller's address. For a known outage the agent gives the cause and estimated restoration time; otherwise the agent asks whether neighbours are out, whether the main breaker was checked and whether anything is down or sparking.

error.defect_description: New outage taken for a known one, or the reverse.

next.condition: new no-power or partial power report
wire down, sparking, pole or tree on line

evidence.note: Author's estimate for an Ontario utility contact centre in 2019-2022 using a CIS, OMS and IVR; no published handle time was found.

steps.name: Give safety instructions and send a priority hazard report
steps.description: The representative tells the caller to stay at least ten metres away and keep others away, creates a priority hazard trouble call in the OMS, and phones the control room when life or property is at risk or police and fire are on site.

error.defect_description: Location described poorly, so the trouble crew searches.

control.basis: Utility public safety procedure for downed or damaged lines: keep-away instruction and immediate dispatch (Ontario Regulation 22/04 public safety obligations)

evidence.note: Ten-metre keep-away is common Ontario utility advice; procedure is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Enter a trouble call in the OMS
steps.description: The representative enters a no-power or partial-power trouble call in the OMS against the customer's premise so that the OMS can group it with other calls and the control room can dispatch, then records the call.

error.defect_description: Call entered on the wrong premise.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for an Ontario utility contact centre in 2019-2022 using a CIS, OMS and IVR; no published handle time was found.

steps.name: Take details of a field service request
steps.description: The representative records what the customer wants: a new or upgraded service, a meter check, a tree near a line, an isolation so a contractor can work safely, or a disconnect for renovation, with the site contact, access and preferred dates.

error.defect_description: Missing access details, so the crew cannot get in.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for an Ontario utility contact centre in 2019-2022 using a CIS, OMS and IVR; no published handle time was found.

steps.name: Create the service order and book an appointment
steps.description: The representative creates the order in the CIS, which passes it to mobile workforce management, offers a four-hour appointment window where the customer must be present, and sends new services to the layout team.

error.defect_description: Wrong order type selected, so the wrong trade is dispatched.

control.basis: OEB Distribution System Code s.7.3-7.4: appointment window of no more than four hours, met 90% of the time

evidence.note: 9,001 appointments in 2021, 98.86% met (src-scorecard); handling time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Warm-transfer the caller to a supervisor
steps.description: When a caller asks for a supervisor or the agent cannot resolve the problem within their authority, the agent places the caller on hold, summarises the case to the supervisor on duty and stays on the line for the introduction.

error.defect_description: Summary leaves out a key fact.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for an Ontario utility contact centre in 2019-2022 using a CIS, OMS and IVR; no published handle time was found.

steps.name: Handle the escalated caller
steps.description: The supervisor listens, reviews the account and earlier contacts, explains the rules that apply, and offers what is within their authority such as a late charge reversal, a longer payment plan or a goodwill credit. Some callers want a formal complaint recorded.

error.defect_description: Credit given outside policy.

control.basis: Contact centre delegation of authority for credits and charge reversals

next.condition: caller asks for a formal complaint

evidence.note: Author's estimate for an Ontario utility contact centre in 2019-2022 using a CIS, OMS and IVR; no published handle time was found.

steps.name: Record a formal complaint
steps.description: The supervisor records the complaint in the CIS complaint log with the facts, the remedy asked for and what was offered, sends the acknowledgement, and assigns it to the complaints team, who must tell the customer about the OEB's complaint process if it is not settled.

error.defect_description: Complaint categorised wrongly.

control.basis: OEB licence and Distribution System Code requirements for a complaint process and written response (s.7.8)

evidence.note: Author's estimate for an Ontario utility contact centre in 2019-2022 using a CIS, OMS and IVR; no published handle time was found.

steps.name: Research the question off the call
steps.description: When the answer needs another department or more digging, the representative promises a callback, then works the case from the queue: reads the bill calculation, asks billing or metering staff by email or Teams, and notes the answer.

error.defect_description: Answer still incomplete.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for an Ontario utility contact centre in 2019-2022 using a CIS, OMS and IVR; no published handle time was found.

steps.name: Call the customer back
steps.description: The representative phones the customer with the answer, leaves a message if there is no reply and tries again the next day, and records the outcome on the account.

error.defect_description: Message left with no clear answer.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for an Ontario utility contact centre in 2019-2022 using a CIS, OMS and IVR; no published handle time was found.

steps.name: Write call notes and the disposition code
steps.description: After the conversation the representative types notes in the CIS contact log and selects the call reason and outcome codes that feed the first-contact-resolution and call-driver reports, then becomes available for the next call.

error.defect_description: Notes too brief or wrong reason code, so the next agent repeats questions.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for an Ontario utility contact centre in 2019-2022 using a CIS, OMS and IVR; no published handle time was found.

steps.name: Review a recorded call for quality
steps.description: A supervisor listens to a sample of recorded calls each week, scores each one against the quality form (verification, accuracy, tone, notes, required disclosures) and coaches the agent on what was missed.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: A few calls per agent per month is common practice; author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Billing dispute needing investigation
exceptions.description: The agent finds a possible error and hands the case to billing analysts, who must reply within 10 business days.

exceptions.name: Callback after research
exceptions.description: The agent cannot answer on the call, researches the question from the queue and calls back a day or two later.

exceptions.name: Escalation and formal complaint
exceptions.description: The caller asks for a supervisor and then for a formal complaint, which goes to the complaints team.

exceptions.name: Public safety hazard
exceptions.description: A wire down or sparking equipment is reported; the agent gives keep-away instructions and sends a priority report.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from call to call closed

evidence.note: Author's estimate: about 8-12 minutes for a typical answered call including queue time; the p90 stays under an hour because only about 5% of calls need callbacks or reviews that take days.

pain_points.description: Storm days bring several times the normal calls; on-time answer fell to 74.6% in 2020 while staff moved to remote work.
About one call in nine is not resolved at first contact, which brings repeat calls and callbacks.

evidence.note: 89.04% first contact resolution in 2021.

pain_points.description: Agents re-key move and service details from calls into separate CIS orders, and wrong premises or dates cause later bills to the wrong person.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

sources.title: Scorecard - Hydro Ottawa Limited (2017-2021) and 2021 Scorecard Management Discussion and Analysis
sources.supports: Telephone calls answered on time 85.07% (2017), 88.74% (2018), 86.15% (2019), 74.60% (2020), 83.14% (2021) against a 65% standard; 186,632 calls to agents in 2021; first contact resolution 84.27-89.88 (2017-2021), 89.04% in 2021 from 3,176 surveyed callers of whom 2,828 said the issue was resolved; billing accuracy 99.88-99.90% against 98%; more than 4.2 million bills in 2021; 9,001 appointments; 95% overall satisfaction.

sources.title: Distribution System Code (consolidated, revised March 27, 2024)
sources.supports: s.2.4.11-2.4.20A security deposit waivers, maximum (billing cycle factor x estimated bill) and instalments over at least 6 months for residential customers; s.2.6.1A monthly billing of residential and GS<50 kW customers (in force December 31, 2016); s.2.6.6.2B payment allocation; s.2.7 arrears payment agreements (down payment up to 15%, 10% for eligible low-income; terms of at least 5 or 10 months, 8, 12 or 16 months for eligible low-income); s.4.2.2.1 disconnection notice not in the bill envelope; s.4.2.2.6 21-day suspension while a LEAP intake agency assesses the customer; s.4.2.3.1 mailed notice deemed received on the fifth day; s.7.6 65% of calls answered in 30 s; s.7.7 abandon rate 10% or less; s.7.8 written response in 10 business days 80% of the time; s.7.10 reconnection within 2 business days 85% of the time; s.7.11 billing accuracy 98% and what counts as an inaccurate bill. Amendment history shows these sections were in force through 2019-2022 apart from the March 2020 changes.

sources.title: The OEB's extended Disconnection Ban will end on July 31, 2020
sources.supports: On March 19, 2020 the OEB extended the winter disconnection ban to July 31, 2020 and widened it to small business customers; after it ended, the account overdue notice, 14-day disconnection notice and LEAP rules applied; COVID-19 Energy Assistance Program (CEAP) one-time on-bill credit applied for through the utility; LEAP emergency assistance and OESP credits.

sources.title: Moving (residential services)
sources.supports: Move requests at least 10 business days before moving day; new customers use an online moving request form and give date of birth, government photo ID and landlord contact; existing customers move or stop service in MyAccount; account set-up charge on the first bill; final bill about three weeks after the move-out date; landlords may not submit for tenants; OESP recipients must re-apply after a move. Page read in 2026; practice in 2019-2022 assumed similar.

assumptions: The unit of work is one call answered by an agent, matching the 186,632 calls a year in the OEB scorecard. Emails, web forms and chat are not counted; they are perhaps 1,500-2,500 more contacts a month (author's estimate) and are part of why stated CSR FTE exceeds the hands-on time.
Hands-on time per call comes to about 9-10 minutes including verification and wrap-up, against the organisation file's note of about 6 minutes; no published handle time was found.

Staffing: hands-on minutes times volume imply fewer FTE than the 27 CSR FTE stated. The gap is time not spent on a call: waiting for calls to arrive (occupancy of about 75-85% is needed to answer 83% in 30 seconds), training, team meetings, Saturday cover and written contacts.
Call reason shares are estimates; the scorecard gives no breakdown.
Queue wait is triangular with low 0, mode 0.05 and high 0.8 minutes so that about 85% of calls are answered within 30 seconds, close to the 2019 and 2021 results.
Roles use the organisation file's ids and loaded costs (wage x 1.40).
Sources were opened on 2026-11-24. The Distribution System Code was read in its March 2024 consolidation; its amendment history shows sections 7.3-7.11 and 2.7 in force throughout 2019-2022.
